title: Black-Hole Signatures in the Finite-Temperature Critical Ising Chain
abstract: We demonstrate that the finite-temperature critical transverse-field Ising chain exhibits quantitative signatures of black-hole physics in its dual gravitational description within the AdS/CFT correspondence. Its finite-temperature dynamics and thermodynamics are consistently captured by a mixed thermal-AdS/BTZ black hole saddle, leading to three mutually compatible observations. First, antipodal excitation transport collapses onto a universal temperature-dependent curve determined by the relative AdS and BTZ contributions to the gravitational partition function, reflecting horizon absorption. Second, in the high-temperature regime, the retarded response exhibits exponential relaxation governed by the lowest quasi-normal mode of the dual black hole. Third, the temperature derivative of the von Neumann entropy develops a pronounced minimum at a temperature consistent with the Hawking-Page transition.
key_claims: Critical Ising chain at finite temperature maps quantitatively to mixed thermal-AdS/BTZ saddle
Antipodal excitation transport shows universal temperature-dependent curve (horizon absorption)
High-temperature relaxation matches BTZ quasi-normal mode spectrum
Von Neumann entropy derivative shows Hawking-Page transition signature
Wang & He follow-up to 2501.03084 (hologron instability paper); same authors, deeper AdS/CFT connection
Transport time T = (pi/2)*l_AdS relation is consistent with BTZ picture in finite-T regime

Supplemental Material S3.A solves the AdS3 null geodesic equations in closed form and proves t_trans = pi for antipodal boundary-to-boundary transport, INDEPENDENTLY of angular momentum M, energy Omega, AND the AdS radius ell (their words: 'independently of the values of M, Omega, and ell').
